description_ru: Ана приходит пожаловаться на шум в одиннадцать вечера и обнаруживает, что её новый сосед очень хорошо играет на барабанах.
text:
Ana: Hello? Is somebody there? I'm sorry to bother you.
Leo: Oh! Hi. Hang on, I can't hear you. Let me take off my headphones. Sorry. Yes?
Ana: I'm Ana. I live in the flat below you, number four.
Leo: Oh. Hi, Ana. I'm Leo. I moved in two weeks ago. Is something wrong?
Ana: Well, it's about the noise. Last night, there was a very loud sound at eleven o'clock. It sounded like somebody was dropping a table.
Leo: Ah. That wasn't a table. That was my drum kit.

Ana: Your drum kit?
Leo: I'm a drummer. Not a famous one yet, but I practise every evening. I thought the walls were thick. Was it very loud?
Ana: My lamp was shaking, Leo. And my cat hid under the bed for two hours.
Leo: Oh no. Poor cat. What's her name?
Ana: His name is Pepper. And he's still angry with me today.
Leo: I'm really sorry. I honestly didn't know. Nobody told me about the walls. The last tenant didn't have any complaints.
Ana: The last tenant was a quiet old lady who played the harp, I think.
Leo: That explains a lot.

Ana: Look, I don't mind music. I like music. But eleven o'clock is too late. I get up at six for work.
Leo: What do you do?
Ana: I'm a baker. I start in the shop at half past six. By eleven o'clock at night, my body is asking for sleep.
Leo: A baker! That's amazing. Do you make bread?
Ana: Bread, rolls and cakes. Why?
Leo: I'm a student, I'm always hungry, and I have very little money. If you want, I'll stop playing after nine, and I'll never complain about the smell of bread.
Ana: Nobody complains about that smell. But nine o'clock sounds fair. Thank you.

Leo: Can I ask one thing? Would you like to hear the drums? Just for a minute? You've only heard them through the floor. It's not the same.
Ana: Now? I came here to complain, and you want to give me a concert.
Leo: A very short concert. Please. Just one song. Then you can go home and feel superior.
Ana: One song. One. And if the walls shake, I'm leaving.
Leo: Deal. Come in. Mind the cables. I'm afraid the flat is a bit of a mess.

Ana: A bit? Leo, there are cymbals in your kitchen, and a sock on the cooker.
Leo: Yes, the sitting room is too small, so the drums live here. Pizza boxes live in the sitting room. It's a long story.
Ana: I don't want to hear it. Okay, play.
Leo: Right. One, two, three, four!
Ana: Wow. That's... not bad. Actually, it's really good. You're fast.
Leo: Thanks! I've practised since I was twelve. My dad bought me my first drums. My mum cried for a month.
Ana: I understand your mum.

Ana: Can I give you some advice?
Leo: Of course.
Ana: Put something soft under the drums. A thick carpet, or an old mattress. It stops the noise going into the floor.
Leo: A mattress? I have one, actually. It's in the corridor. Somebody left it there.
Ana: Then you have your answer. And ask the shop downstairs if they've got old boxes. Egg boxes on the wall help a bit too.
Leo: Egg boxes? You're joking. Where do I find forty of them?
Ana: Ask me. The bakery uses a hundred eggs a day. I'll bring you a bag tomorrow.
Ana: I'm not joking. Musicians do it everywhere. My brother plays the trumpet, and my parents' house looks like a chicken farm.
Leo: That's the best advice I've had all month.

Leo: Ana, would you like a cup of tea? I owe you one for the cat.
Ana: Only if you stop calling it "the cat". His name is Pepper.
Leo: Sorry. Pepper. Would you like some tea, and would Pepper like to come up for a visit? I have a lot of cables to play with.
Ana: He'd destroy them in five minutes. But maybe next week. I could bring some rolls for you.
Leo: That's a trade I'll take.
Ana: And, Leo, when do you play your first concert? I might come and listen.
Leo: In March, at a little pub called The Blue Anchor. Come and bring Pepper. He can wear earplugs.
Ana: I'll bring earplugs for me, too. See you soon, drummer.
Leo: See you, neighbour. And thank you, really. You could have called the landlord.
Ana: I thought about it. But then I heard the drums, and I changed my mind. Anybody who plays like that deserves a second chance.
Leo: Even at eleven at night?
Ana: Not at eleven at night. Nine o'clock, Leo. Nine!

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Кончик языка не касается нёба и не вибрирует; не раскатывайте русское «р».
Короткий звук между «а» и «э», рот полуоткрыт; не произносите «о».
Рот открыт шире, чем для «э»; звук между «э» и «а».
Начните с «э» и плавно перейдите в «и»; это один слитный звук.

questions.question: Why does Ana come to Leo's flat?
questions.answer: To complain about the noise from his drums late at night.

questions.question: What does Ana advise Leo to put under the drums?
questions.answer: A mattress or a thick carpet.

questions.question: Where will Leo play his first concert?
questions.answer: At a pub called The Blue Anchor.
